1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface at comfortable sizes with ample line height, though letter spacing is default rather than explicitly widened.

2.why: No italics, all-caps sentences, or dense paragraphs appear anywhere; every instruction is a short title-case sentence.

3.why: Content sits in a narrow single centered column with large text and full-width controls that would fit a phone viewport, although only desktop-width screenshots were supplied.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Use an authenticator app to generate a code.' are single plain-language sentences without jargon.

5.why: Only the recovery-code field shows a format placeholder (ABCDE-23489) and the pre-filled email/phone demonstrate their format, while the verification-code and authenticator-code inputs give no example of the expected value.

6.why: The longest text on any screen is a two-sentence notice, so the user is never forced to read a long block of text to proceed.

7.why: No copy buttons are provided; the setup screen says 'Add this value manually,' and every code (verification, authenticator, recovery) must be hand-typed into plain inputs.

8.why: The authenticator setup offers only a raw secret and otpauth URI with the instruction to add it manually; no QR code or equivalent alternative is shown.

9.why: Code fields are plain text inputs with no visible one-time-code autofill support, and there is no password field for a password manager to fill.

10.why: Each screen pairs a bold heading with a prominent solid-blue primary button, though step 08 shows two identical blue buttons that blur which action is primary.

11.why: Every step requests a single primary action except step 08, where 'Verify recovery code' and 'Generate replacement codes' appear together as coequal blue buttons.

12.why: Notices such as 'Authenticator created. Add this value manually.' and 'Recovery code confirmed.' plainly state what happened and what to do next, though returning to the sign-in screen after logout only implies the session ended.

13.why: The error screen invites retry ('Please try again') with no lockout and recovery codes can be regenerated, although regeneration consumes an unused code and no reveal/hide toggle exists.

14.why: The only observed error, 'Unable to complete this request. Please try again.', is non-blaming but never explains what the problem actually was.

15.why: No countdown or reading timeout is visible on any screen, and the otpauth URI's period=120 allows a generous two minutes per authenticator code.
